business_problem: The company needed to forecast demand and manage warehouse inventory more accurately so stock-value losses caused by changing market demand could be reduced.
solution_summary: Capgemini and Google Cloud built a two-part AI decision layer for a global conglomerate's warehouse and demand-planning operations. The program started with a pilot market so the team could prove the design before wider rollout. Historical sales and stock data feed a forecast engine that projects demand over 30-, 60-, 90-day, and annual windows, while a generative AI chatbot built on Google Vertex AI interprets user intent, writes database queries on the fly, and returns answers as text, charts, tables, and graphics. Together, those services give planners both forward-looking demand signals and conversational access to the underlying inventory picture, letting the business identify where stock value is at risk, react earlier to market shifts, and make warehouse decisions that protect margins rather than relying on delayed manual analysis.

solution_components.name: Google Vertex AI
solution_components.role: Runs the large language model capabilities behind the conversational assistant.

solution_components.name: Generative AI-based chatbot
solution_components.role: Lets users query inventory and demand data interactively and receive answers in multiple business-friendly formats.

solution_components.name: Forecast engine
solution_components.role: Generates 30-, 60-, 90-day, and annual sales and demand forecasts from historical data.

data_flow: Historical sales and stock data are analyzed by the forecast engine to project demand windows, while users send natural-language questions to the Vertex AI chatbot. The chatbot generates database queries, pulls the relevant inventory context, and returns text, tables, charts, and graphics that planners combine with forecasts to optimize warehouse and supply-chain decisions.
integration_points: Database queries generated on the fly
business_outcome: The pilot gave the conglomerate clearer demand signals, better visibility into stock-value risk, and a scalable pattern for warehouse optimization that can be rolled out to additional countries and facilities.
